full_judgment:
On an application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. 1958, the accused-petitioner has challenged legality of the order dated 7-3-2013 passed by the learned Special Judge, Special Court No.3, Dhaka, rejecting the application to stay further proceedings of Special Case No.17 of 2011 arising out of ACC GR Case No.83 of 2009 corresponding to Cantonment Police Station Case No.8 dated 26-10-2009. 

 7. Mr AKM Fakhrul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner though argued that the evidence of one case can- not be used in another case and since the accused- petitioner convicted in Special Case No. 1 of 2008 under section 27(1) of the Anti-corruption Commission Ain, 2004 for the same amount of money, trial of the Special Case No. 17 of 2011 is barred under Article 35(2) of the constitution, section 403 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also under section 26 of the General Clauses Act. 1897, but he mainly advanced his arguments on point of maintainability of the case. He submitted that the ordinance No. VII of 2007 and ordinance No. VIII by which the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain. 2002, was incorporated in schedule of the Anti-corruption Commission Act. 2004 and Criminal Law Amendment Act. 1958, were not placed before the parliament for its endorsement as an Act of Parliament as per Provision of Article 93 of the constitution. So, the said ordinances ceased to exist on and from 24th February, 2009 and as such proceeding under the said ordinances is illegal and beyond jurisdiction of the special Judge. He also submitted that the offences, as alleged in the ejahar, have been com- mitted during the period from 1-1-2003 to 31-5-2007 but the ejahar was lodged on 26-10-2009 under the provision of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain 2009, which saved only the proceedings pending under the provisions of Money Laundering Protirodh Ordinance, 2008 and the said ordinance saved only the proceedings pending under the provisions of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002. Mr Islam submitted that since no proceeding was pending under the Ain 2002, till it was repealed on 15-8- 2008 by the ordinance of 2008, the offences even if committed are not saved either by the ordinance of 2008 or by the Ain 2009 and as such the proceeding is illegal. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney-General appearing for the State submitted that there is no merit in the submissions advanced on behalf of the accused-petitioner since those points were settled by our Apex Court in the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18, arises out of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal no. 10 of 2011 and also in the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 162, arises out of Civil Review Petition No.32 of 2011. He also submitted that the accused-petitioner raised the question of maintainability on these point in Criminal Revision No. 1 of 2013 by filing an application under section l0 (1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, and the application was summarily rejected vide order dated 17-1-2013 by a bench of this Court. 

 12. On perusal of the judgment of the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh &Others, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18, arises out of Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No.10 of 2011 and also the judgment of the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reportedin 63 DLR (AD) 162, arises out of Civil Review Petition No. 32, it appears that the questions raised by the accused-petitioner in this application relating to repeal of the ordinance Nos. VII and VIII, saving clause, saving under section 6 of the General Clause Act and period of the offence were answered clearly and elaborately by our apex Court. It is pertinent to be mentioned here that the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner submitted at length but did not refer the case of Tarique Rahman vs Bangladesh Government, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 162, arises out of Civil Review Petition No. 32 of 2011. Even it is not disclosed in the application that this accused-petitioner filed another application under section 10(1 A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 wherein also the question of maintainability of the proceeding was raised almost on similar ground and the application was rejected summarily. Before that the present accused-petitioner unsuccessfully moved an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash the proceeding of the case before this Division.
